chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboub, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Abbas ibn Aamir, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad Al-Musli, from Abu Muhammad, from Imran, from Saeed ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a dispute occurs between two men, two angels descend and say to the foolish one of the two: 'You spoke, and you spoke, and you are deserving of what you said; you will be recompensed for what you said.' And they say to the forbearing one of the two: 'You were patient and forbearing; Allah will forgive you if you complete that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But if the forbearing one replies to him, the two angels ascend.'
ai.seo_question: What happens spiritually when two people argue and one remains patient?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the metaphysical reward for *hilm* (forbearance) during conflict, a core virtue in Shia ethics emphasizing self-restraint as a means of divine favor. The descending angels symbolize immediate spiritual validation, while the condition that the angels ascend if the forbearing party replies underscores the fragility and preciousness of maintaining silence in the face of provocation. This narrative reinforces the scholarly view that true victory lies in enduring the dispute with grace rather than engaging in reciprocal argumentation.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Mahboub, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Abbas Bin Aamir, deom Rabie Bin Muhammad Al Musly, from Abu Muhammad, from Imran, from Saeed Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a dispute occurs between two men, two Angels descend, and they are both saying to the foolish one from the two, ‘You talk, and you talk, and you are deserving of what you say. You will soon be Recompensed due to what you say’. And they are both saying to the forbearing one of the two, ‘You were patient, and you were forbearing. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Forgiving (your sins) for you if you complete (upon) that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But if the forbearing one replies against him, the two Angels ascend’.
en.sarwar: 9. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ayyub ibn Nuh from ‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir from Rabi’ ibn Muhammad al-Musalli from abu Muhammad from ‘Imran from Sa’id ibn Yasar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When two men dispute each other, two angels come down and say to the foolish one of the two, ‘You said what you said and you were the kind to say what you said and you will be brought to account for what you have said.’ Then they will say to the forbearing one of the two men, ‘You exercised patience and forbearance. Allah will forgive you if you will complete it.’ The Imam said, ‘If the forbearing man answers back to the other man the two angels will ascend.’”
